posts.caption: Black Gram Vada (Prasad Style)
posts.fullCaption:
Black Gram Vada (Prasad Style)

Traditionally offered as Prasad in Hanuman and Venkateswara Balaji temples, often strung together as Vada Mala garlands for Hanuman . 

The crisp bite, peppery aroma, and ghee‑infused flavor make them a favorite both in temples and homes. 

Ingredients

• 500 g black gram (whole or split black urad dal)
• 50 ml ghee
• 2 tsp (≈12 g) salt
• 2 tsp (≈5 g) cumin seeds
• 3 tsp (≈11 g) black pepper
• Pinch of hing (asafoetida)

Method

1. Place the black gram in hot water for 30–45 minutes only. Do not over‑soak.
2. Drain completely and grind coarsely without adding water , with salt ,cumin, black pepper, and hing.
3. Heat ghee until hot, pour it over the mixture, and mix well.
4.Take small portions, roll into balls, and press flat on a baking sheet or plate to desired thickness. .

* Thin vadas → crispier texture
* Thicker vadas → softer inside

5. Deep fry on medium flame until golden brown.

#vada #blackgramvada #hanumanmala❤️ #southindianprasadams #manthafood #ManthaFood

posts.caption: 🌱 Coriander Rice (Khotimeera Annam)
posts.fullCaption:
🌱 Coriander Rice (Khotimeera Annam)

✨ A fragrant, flavorful rice dish that’s quick to make - Can be enjoyed as it is or pairs beautifully with yogurt or dal.

Ingredients
• 200 g rice (cook & cool )
• 3–4 green chilies (adjust to taste)
• 3–4 garlic cloves
• 2 tbsp white sesame
• 100 g fresh coriander leaves
• 2 tbsp oil
• 2 tsp salt

Tempering:
• 1 tsp urad dal
• 1 tsp chana dal

Method
1. Heat oil, fry chilies & garlic lightly.
2. Add sesame, fry till golden.
3. Add chopped coriander leaves, sauté 2 mins. Cool & coarsely grind.
4. In a pan, heat oil, fry urad & chana dal till golden.
5. Add ground coriander mix + salt, sauté briefly.
6. Mix in rice, toss well.

posts.caption: Crispy Ragi Spinach Balls
posts.fullCaption:
Crispy Ragi Spinach Balls

Love the earthy goodness of ragi? These balls are crispy outside, soft inside, and perfect to enjoy plain as they are or with peanut chutney, pickle, or your favorite sauce. Best eaten hot for crunch, though they turn soft and comforting when cool. You can also add spinach, grated carrot, or grated bottle gourd for extra flavor and nutrition.
Ingredients
• 1 glass ragi flour
• 1 glass sour buttermilk
• 1 glass water
• 3–4 green chilies, finely chopped
• 1 medium onion, finely chopped
• 1 bunch spinach, blanched & chopped
• A handful of coriander leaves, finely chopped
• 2–3 tbsp oil
Method
1. In a pan, mix ragi flour, buttermilk, water, green chilies, onion, spinach, coriander, and oil.
2. Cook on medium flame, stirring continuously, until it forms a firm dough. Keep adding a little oil to avoid sticking.
3. Cover and let it rest until warm.
4. Knead well, then shape into small balls.
5. Cook by one of these methods:• Air fry at 170°C for 10–12 minutes
• Deep fry until golden brown
• Shallow fry in a pan with little oil.

posts.fullCaption:
Air-Fried Crispy Poha
A light, crunchy, and flavorful snack made with minimal ingredients—healthy, tasty, and absolutely addictive! Perfect for tea-time, travel, or guilt-free munching anytime.

Ingredients
• 250 g poha (flattened rice)
• 1 cup peanuts (75 g)
• 1 cup cashews (75 g)
• 1 cup roasted chana dal (50 g)
• 8–10 green chillies, slit lengthwise
• A handful of curry leaves
• 2 tbsp oil
• ½ tsp hing (asafoetida)
• ¼ tsp turmeric powder
• Salt to taste
(Optional: add makhana and puffed rice for extra crunch)
Method
1. Air-fry separately at 180°C:
• Poha: 5–8 minutes until crisp
• Peanuts & cashews: 5 minutes until golden
• Roasted chana dal: 2 minutes

2. Prepare seasoning:
• Heat oil in a pan.
• Fry green chillies until slightly crisp.
• Add curry leaves; fry until crunchy.
• Stir in hing and turmeric.

3. Mix & coat:
•Combine roasted poha, peanuts, cashews, and chana dal.
• Add salt and seasoning.
• Toss well until evenly coated.

posts.caption: Crispy Sesame (Til) Chikki – Traditional Sweet Treat
posts.fullCaption:
Crispy Sesame (Til) Chikki – Traditional Sweet Treat
This is one of my all‑time favorites! I’ve always bought sesame (til) chikki from stores, but tried making it at home for the first time — and wow, it tastes so fresh, good, and crispy. Truly one of the easiest sweets to make!
You can also add sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, or peanuts for extra crunch and flavor.
Ingredients
• 150 g roasted sesame seeds (til)
(gas top / 180°C – 5 mins)
• 100 g jaggery
• ¼ cup water (≈ 50 ml)
• 1 tsp ghee
1. Add water and jaggery to a pan.
• Boil until jaggery melts.
• If impurities appear, strain and return to the pan.
• Continue boiling until it reaches a soft , firm ball consistency (test by dropping a little syrup in cold water — it should form a firm ball).
2. Mix with Sesame• Add roasted sesame seeds to the hot jaggery syrup.
• Stir quickly so all seeds are evenly coated. Cook for 1-2 mins.
3. Grease a plate with ghee and transfer the mixture.
• Place a greased paper or plate on top and press to desired thickness.
• Alternatively, grease a rolling pin and roll while mixture is still medium hot.
4. Cut or Shape• While still warm, mark lines for cutting.
• Once cooled, break into pieces.
• Optionally, grease your hands and shape into til laddus (balls) while mixture is safe to handle.
Tips
• Always test jaggery syrup consistency; undercooked syrup makes sticky chikki, overcooked makes it too hard.
• Store in an airtight container to keep crisp.

posts.caption: Minty Chana Yogurt Bowl
posts.fullCaption:
Minty Chana Yogurt Bowl
A refreshing, protein-packed snack bursting with flavor and crunch!

Ingredients:
• 1 cup cooked chickpeas (chana)
• 1 tbsp coriander-mint chutney
• 2 tbsp thick yogurt
• ½ cup finely chopped cucumber
• 1 tomato, chopped
• 1 small onion, chopped
• ½ tsp chaat masala
Method:
1. Soak chana overnight and pressure cook for 3–4 whistles with a pinch of salt.
2. In a bowl, take 1 cup of boiled chana.
3. Add coriander mint chutney, yogurt, cucumber, tomato, and onion.
4. Mix everything well until coated.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala on top.
6. Serve chilled or at room temperature. Enjoy the burst of flavors !

After a little break, I’m back with a quick and delicious treat that’s perfect for snacking or everyday cravings! This crunchy makhana recipe tastes just like caramel popcorn—but with a wholesome desi twist. Ready in minutes, and totally addictive!

Caramel Makhana Crunch
Ingredients:
• Makhana (Fox Nuts) – 100 g
• Til (Sesame Seeds) – 50 g
• Jaggery – 150 g
• Ghee – 1 tsp
• Water – ½ cup
Instructions:
1. Dry roast makhana and sesame seeds separately in an air fryer or on gas.
* Makhana should be crispy.
* Sesame seeds should turn light brown and aromatic.
2. In a wide pan, add water and grated jaggery.
* Simmer on low flame until it thickens and forms sticky drops from the ladle.
3. Add ghee, roasted sesame, and makhana. Mix well to coat evenly.
4. Transfer to a plate while still warm (or it may stick to the pan).
5. Let it cool completely and store in an airtight container.
Ready in minutes, this crunchy delight is perfect for guilt-free snacking!

Palli podi 
Palli Podi a delicious and versatile spice blend! Can be eaten with hot rice and ghee, idli , dosa or as a seasoning for veggies and poha. The aroma and taste are incredible!

Ingredients
- 250gms peanuts
- 1 tablespoon (20gms) chili powder
- 4-5 dry red chilies
- 2 teaspoons (5gms) cumin seeds (Jeera)
- 2 tablespoons (10gms) coriander seeds (Dhania)
- 3 tablespoons (30gms) sesame seeds (TIL)
- 5-6 cloves garlic (20gms) (optional)
- 2 teaspoons (12gms) salt
- 2 tablespoons (15gms) dry coconut (optional)

1. Dry roast the peanuts, in oven (180C 12-15 mins) or gas top on medium flame 
2.Dry sesame seeds and dry red chillies in a pan until fragrant.
3. Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds for 1- 2 mins and desiccated coconut ( few secs)
4. Let them cool completely.
5. Grind the mixture into a coarse powder.
5. Add the chili powder , salt and garlic to the powder and grind a bit. 
7. Store the Palli Podi in an airtight container.

posts.fullCaption:
Perugu Vankaya (South Indian-style Dahi Baingan) A deliciously creamy, tangy brinjal (eggplant) curry with a South Indian twist — a perfect comfort dish to pair with hot rice or rotis!
Ingredients: Vegetables:
* Brinjal (eggplant) – 250 gms, sliced lengthwise
* Onion – 1, sliced lengthwise
For Marination:
* Thick yogurt – 1 small cup (100gms)
* Besan (gram flour) – 1 tablespoon
* Turmeric powder – ¼ tsp
* Ginger-garlic paste – 1 tablespoon
* Salt – ¼ tsp (or to taste)
* Coriander powder – 1 tbsp
* Cumin powder – ½ tbsp
* Jeerakharam (or red chili powder) – 1 tbsp
* A little oil for coating
Tempering:
* Mustard seeds – ½ tsp
* Cumin seeds – ½ tsp
* A pinch of hing (asafoetida)
* Curry leaves
Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk the yogurt with besan until smooth. Add ginger-garlic paste and all the dry spices. Mix well.
2. In another large bowl, toss the brinjal and onions with a little salt and oil. Add the yogurt-spice mixture and coat everything well.
3. Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds. Once they splutter, add cumin seeds, hing, and curry leaves.
4. Add the marinated brinjal-onion mix. Cover and cook on medium flame until the brinjal turns soft.
5. Remove the lid and cook uncovered till the oil separates and the gravy thickens. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.Tips:
* If using a steel pan, stir frequently and cook on low-medium heat if using less oil.

posts.caption: Homemade Indian Yogurt (Curd/Dahi) Yogurt is an everyday essential in almost every South Indian meal! While…
posts.fullCaption:
Homemade Indian Yogurt (Curd/Dahi) Yogurt is an everyday essential in almost every South Indian meal! While it may seem simple to many Indians, this recipe is especially for my lovely Chinese friends who enjoy Indian yogurt and want to try making it at home.
Ingredients:
* 1 cup fresh milk (full cream or low fat)
* 1 tbsp fresh yogurt (as a starter culture)
Method:
1. Boil the milk thoroughly—this step is crucial whether you’re using fresh cow milk or pasteurized milk.
2. Allow the milk to cool until it’s warm (not hot). Optionally, strain the milk to remove the thick cream layer.
3. Add 1 tablespoon of fresh yogurt to the warm milk and stir gently.
4. Cover the bowl and keep it in a warm place for 5–6 hours or until the yogurt sets. (Setting time depends on your room temperature.)
5. For a quicker set, place a dry red chili on top—an age-old traditional tip!
Note: A good starter culture is key! The best results come from fresh, well-set yogurt. If you don’t have any, you can make a basic culture by adding a few drops of lemon juice or a slit green chili to warm milk. Let it sit in a warm spot for around 12 hours until it curdles. This can be used as a starter for your first batch—though it’s not suitable for eating on its own.

posts.caption: Bellam Pulusu (Mukkala Pulusu)
posts.fullCaption:
Bellam Pulusu (Mukkala Pulusu)
A must-have in every South Indian wedding lunch and important event! This traditional Pulusu is a perfect balance of sweet, sour, and spicy flavors, pairing beautifully with rice. The best combo? Muddapappu or Nuvvulu Podi! Add bottle gourd, pumpkin, or sweet potato for extra deliciousness.
Ingredients:
* Vegetables (adjust as needed):
 * Handful of small sambar onions
 * 1 drumstick (cut into pieces)
 * 1 carrot (cut into pieces)
 * 1 brinjal (cut long)
 * 2 green chilies (slit)
 * 3-4 ladies’ fingers
 * 1 bunch Malabar spinach (Bachali Kura)
* Other ingredients:
 * 1 tsp turmeric
 * 1 lemon-sized tamarind (soaked, juice extracted)
 * 1 tbsp rice flour (for thickening)
 * 1 tbsp Menthi Gunda (or substitute with ½ tsp roasted methi powder + pinch of hing)
 * 1 tbsp jaggery
 * Salt to taste
 * Coriander leaves (for garnishing)
Tempering:
* 1 tsp oil
* 1 tsp mustard seeds
* ½ tsp cumin seeds
* 1 dry red chili
* ½ tsp hing
* Few curry leaves
* 1 tsp chili powder (optional)
For Menthi Gunda Powder (store and use as needed):
* ½ glass urad dal (minappu)
* 1 glass coriander seeds
* ¼ glass cumin seeds
* ¼ glass fenugreek seeds (methi)
* 5-6 dry red chilies
* Little hing
* Little salt
Method:
In a pot, cook all the vegetables with turmeric, tamarind extract, and salt until almost done. If using ladies’ fingers, add them at the end.Simmer for a few minutes.
Mix rice flour with a little water and add it to the pulusu for thickening. Stir in jaggery and menthi gunda. Let it cook for a few more minutes.Prepare tempering: Heat oil, add mustard seeds, cumin, red chili, hing, and curry leaves. Pour this over the pulusu.
Garnish with coriander leaves .

posts.caption: Pakam Chalividi
posts.fullCaption:
Pakam Chalividi
Posting after a long break 🤭! Back now with something special – Pakam Chalividi.
Pakam Chalividi is a traditional South Indian sweet with deep cultural significance. It is customary to prepare and offer this sweet to married daughters visiting their mother’s home before they return to their own. This heartfelt gesture symbolizes the mother’s wish for her daughter’s happiness and prosperity, and the sweet often becomes a token of love for the daughter to take back to her home. When made the right way, it transforms into an irresistible treat. My mom makes it the best, and it’s one of my absolute favorites! Ingredients : * 2 glasses of rice (yields approximately 4 glasses of rice flour)
* 1.5 glasses of sugar/jaggery
* 1 glass of water
* 2 tbsp cardamom powder
* 1 medium coconut (finely chopped into small pieces)
* 1 small glass sesame seeds
* 1/4 cup ghee (approximately) 
 * **Always prepare an extra 1/2 glass of rice flour. If the mixture becomes too runny, you can add more flour to adjust the consistency.

posts.fullCaption:
Happy New Year 2025! 🎉 Starting the year with a bang—and a challenge! The first recipe of the year is the intricate and delightful Chakkilalu. A traditional snack that’s as tricky as it is tasty, but totally worth the effort. Let’s roll into the new year with crispy perfection! 😁
Ingredients
* Rice flour: 2 cups (freshly made as described below)
* Carom seeds (Ajwain): 1/2 tsp
* Sesame seeds: 1 small cup
* Salt: 1 tsp (adjust to taste)
* Chili powder (optional): To taste
* Water: Approx. 3/4 cup (adjust as needed)
Making Fresh Rice Flour :Use rice that is slightly glutinous and not too old or new. This ensures the right consistency. Soak the rice in water for 3-4 hours.Strain the water and spread the rice on a soft cotton cloth. Let it dry for 15-30 minutes until the water is fully absorbed but the rice remains slightly damp.Grind the damp rice into a fine powder. Use a fine sieve twice to ensure the powder is smooth.Use the fresh flour immediately or sun-dry it completely to remove any moisture. (Note: Moist flour can cause oil splatter or bursting during frying. Be cautious!)n a large bowl, mix the rice flour with carom seeds, sesame seeds, and salt.Gradually add water to form a loose dough. The dough should neither be hard nor too sticky. Adjust the consistency by adding water or flour as needed.Shaping the Chakkilalu: Prepare a few layers of cotton cloth to place the rolled Chakkilalu on.Take a small portion of dough and roll it into a circle using your fingers. Typically, roll it into three concentric circles, ensuring the end aligns with the start.Place the shaped Chakkilalu on the cloth and let them dry until all the moisture is absorbed. They should lift easily from the cloth once dried.
Frying : Heat oil in a deep pan on medium flame.Carefully drop the dried Chakkilalu into the hot oil. Cover the pan for the first few seconds to avoid oil splatter if any moisture remains.Fry until they turn a golden brown.Practice rolling the dough to get the perfect shape, as it can be tricky initially.#Chakkilalu #SouthIndianSnacks #TraditionalRecipes #CrispyDelights #IndianFestiveSnacks #HomemadeGoodness #SesameSnacks #DeepFriedSnacks #ManthaFood

posts.caption: Kachori Recipe
posts.fullCaption:
Kachori Recipe
This is a special kachori recipe shared by my good friend Vijaya Lakshmi Birla, who is an expert in making them and is known for preparing the best kachoris and rasgullas—which she taught me too! Follow this recipe for perfectly flaky, crispy kachoris with a flavorful moong dal stuffing.
Ingredients
For the Dough (Cover):
* 3 cups maida (all-purpose flour)
* ½ cup ghee
* ½ tsp salt
* ½ to ⅔ cup warm water (adjust as needed)
For the Stuffing:
* 1 cup moong dal (200 gms, soaked 8-10 hours)
* ½ tsp salt (adjust to taste)
* ½ tsp hing (asafoetida)
* 2 tsp garam masala
* 2 tsp chili powder
* 3-4 finely chopped green chili (optional)
* 1 tsp jeera (cumin) powder
* 2 tsp crushed coriander seeds or powder
* 1 tbsp crushed saunf (fennel seeds)
* 1 tsp black salt
* 1 tsp aamchur (dry mango powder)
* 2 tbsp besan (gram flour)
* Oil (for frying and cooking)

1. Preparing the Dough:
* Mix maida, ghee, and salt in a bowl until crumbly.
* Gradually add warm water to knead a soft, slightly sticky dough (softer than roti dough).
* Cover and rest for 20-25 minutes.
* Knead again for 5-10 minutes, adjusting consistency with water or flour if needed.
2. Preparing the Stuffing:
* Step 1: Boil soaked moong dal for 10-15 minutes.
 * Remove 70% cooked dal (dal 1) and set aside.
 * Cook the remaining dal (dal 2) until soft (it should powder when pressed).
* Step 2: Heat oil, add hing and besan, and fry for 2 minutes.
* Add dal 2 and cook, stirring continuously while adding oil little by little to prevent sticking.
* Mix in dal 1 and spices: salt, garam masala, chili powder, jeera powder, coriander, saunf, and black salt.
* Finish with aamchur, cool the mixture, and form small stuffing balls.
3. Assembling the Kachoris and Frying :

posts.caption: Vankaya Pachi Pulusu
posts.fullCaption:
Vankaya Pachi Pulusu
A flavorful dish made with the water leftover from boiling vegetables like brinjals, ladies’ finger, or bitter gourd enhanced with tamarind, jaggery, and spices. Perfect with white rice or mudda pappu.

Ingredients
For the Base:
* Water used for boiling brinjals (from Vankaya Kobbari Kharam recipe)*
* 1 tbsp nuvvula podi (dry-roasted sesame seeds and red chili, ground coarsely)
* 1 tsp jaggery or sugar (adjust to taste)
* Finely chopped coriander leaves
For Tempering:
* ½ tsp mustard seeds
* 2–4 fenugreek seeds
* ½ dry red chili
* ½ tsp oil
* 1–2 green chilies, finely chopped
* A few curry leaves

Instructions
1. Prepare the Base:
 * Use the water leftover from boiling brinjals (boiled with turmeric, tamarind, and salt).
 * Taste the water and adjust the salt, tamarind, or consistency by adding regular water, if necessary.
 * Stir in jaggery and nuvvula podi. Mix until well combined.
2. Make the Tempering:
 * Heat oil in a small pan.
 * Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and dry red chili. Allow the mustard seeds to splutter.
 * Add finely chopped green chilies and curry leaves. Sauté for a few seconds until aromatic.
3. Combine:
 * Pour the tempering over the prepared water mixture. Mix well.
4. Garnish and Serve:
 * Add finely chopped coriander leaves for garnish.

*Note: The water should already have a base flavor from tamarind, salt, and turmeric, so adjust seasoning accordingly.

posts.caption: Vankaya Kobbari Kharam (Stuffed Brinjal)
posts.fullCaption:
Vankaya Kobbari Kharam (Stuffed Brinjal)
A lighter, garlic-optional variation of Guttu Vankaya that’s easy to digest, crispy on the outside, and soft inside.

Ingredients
For the Brinjals:
* 8–10 small brinjals (eggplants)
* 1 small lemon-sized ball of tamarind (juiced)
* ½ tsp turmeric powder
* Salt, to taste
For the Stuffing:
* 1 cup fresh or dry coconut
* 3–4 garlic cloves (optional)
* 1 tbsp coriander seeds
* 2–3 dried red chilies
* Oil (for shallow frying)

Method
1. Prepare the Brinjals:
 * Wash and slit the brinjals crosswise without cutting them completely.
 * In a pan, add water, tamarind juice, turmeric powder, and salt.
 * Place the slit brinjals in the pan, cover, and cook until they are soft.
 * Drain the brinjals and set them aside. (Reserve the water for making Pachi Pulusu, a tamarind-based dish.)
2. Make the Stuffing:
 * Dry roast coriander seeds, garlic (if using), and coconut until light brown.
 * Add red chili powder, a pinch of salt, and grind the mixture into a coarse paste.
3. Stuff and Fry:
 * Fill each brinjal with the prepared stuffing.
 * Heat oil in a pan for shallow frying. Place the stuffed brinjals in the pan and fry until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides.
 * Sprinkle any leftover stuffing on top for added flavour.

posts.caption: Masala Cashew Recipe
posts.fullCaption:
Masala Cashew Recipe

For nut lovers, this is a quick and easy recipe to make at home. Freshly spiced and full of flavour, these masala cashews are a perfect snack to enjoy anytime!

Ingredients:
* 250 gms cashews
* 1 tbsp ghee
* 2 tbsp Karivepaku podi (curry leaf powder) https://www.instagram.com/reel/Cxwm_HCSzkK/?igsh=MW5qeTVrZTJ1dzIxdQ==
* 1 tbsp jeera kharam (spicy cumin powder) https://www.instagram.com/reel/Cvb_tqjJOum/?igsh=MTJrZmJjZ25zZ2Z5dg==
* 1/2 tsp salt
Instructions:
1. Prepare the Cashews:
 * Oven Method: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Spread the cashews evenly on a baking sheet and bake for 10-12 minutes, until they’re lightly golden. Keep an eye on them to prevent burning.
 * Stovetop Method: If you prefer not to use the oven, heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan over medium-low flame. Add the cashews and fry, stirring occasionally, until they turn golden. Be careful not to burn them.
2. Season the Cashews: Remove the cashews from the oven or pan and let them cool slightly. While still warm, add a little extra ghee if needed and toss well until all the cashews are evenly coated.
3. Add Spices: Sprinkle the Karivepaku podi, jeera kharam, and salt over the cashews. Mix thoroughly to ensure the spices coat the cashews evenly.
Note: If you don’t have Karivepaku podi or jeera kharam, you can substitute with your favorite spice blend.

posts.caption: Chimmili (Sesame/Til Ladoo)
posts.fullCaption:
Chimmili (Sesame/Til Ladoo)
This is a simple, healthy, and delicious sweet that can be made in just a few minutes, using only 2-3 ingredients. Perfect for satisfying sweet cravings!
Ingredients:
* 1 cup sesame seeds
* 1/2 cup jaggery (grated) or powdered sugar
* 1-2 tablespoons ghee (optional)
Method:
1. Dry roast the sesame seeds: Heat a pan over medium flame and dry roast the sesame seeds for about 2 minutes, just until the raw smell disappears. Make sure not to over-roast them. Allow them to cool.
2. Grind the sesame seeds: Once the sesame seeds have cooled, grind them coarsely in a blender.
3. Mix with jaggery or sugar: Add the grated jaggery (or powdered sugar) to the coarsely ground sesame seeds. Mix thoroughly, ensuring there are no lumps, especially if using jaggery.
4. Form the ladoos:
 * With ghee: Add 1-2 tablespoons of ghee to the mixture to help bind it and roll the mixture into balls. The addition of ghee not only helps with shaping but also enhances the shelf life of the ladoos.
 * Without ghee: If you prefer not to use ghee, lightly sprinkle water over the mixture. With wet hands, form the mixture into balls.
Note: Ghee makes the ladoos last longer, but water can be a quick alternative if you’re looking for a lighter version.
